# fastf 3.8.0 — the todo list grows up

A project's task list was the one thing fastf could read and write that only
the guided app could reach, and a long one was a single undifferentiated
column. This release gives it phases, a command line, a template that can hand
it out, and machine-readable output for everything.

Nothing about an existing project changes. A list with no phases behaves
exactly as it did, every `PROJECT_INFO.md`, `config.toml` and template works
untouched, and no flag or file format was removed.

## Phases

A `###` line inside `## Todo` labels the tasks under it, until the next one:

```markdown
## Todo

- [x] read the order

### Main Edit
- [ ] cut the first minute
- [ ] colour grade

### Other
```

The detail pane draws each label over the run it names. A label is not a task,
so it takes no number, ticking is unaffected, and a list that has none looks
exactly as it always did. Write them when a list grows long enough to want
them.

## `fastf todo`

```bash
fastf todo list ID0047                            # numbered, grouped by phase
fastf todo list ID0047 --open                     # only what is left
fastf todo add ID0047 "colour grade"
fastf todo add ID0047 "cut" --phase "Main Edit"   # under a label
fastf todo done ID0047 3                          # tick number 3
fastf todo done ID0047 3 --undo
```

`--phase` adds to the end of that label's run, matching the name whatever its
case, and opens the label when there is none by that name — above an
`### Other` if the list has one, at the end otherwise. `done` reads the list
first and refuses if that task changed meanwhile, rather than ticking the wrong
line, and ticking what is already ticked writes nothing.

## Machine-readable output

```bash
fastf recent --json | jq '.[].id'
fastf search tag:draft --json
fastf show ID0047            # one project, the summary a person reads
fastf show ID0047 --json     # the same project, whole
```

`--json` prints a bare array and never opens the picker. `fastf show` is new:
one project's facts, its template variables, its notes, and its todos with the
phase each sits under. The shape is a promise — fields get added, not renamed.

## A template can hand out its task list

```yaml
todo:
  - tasks:
      - "read the brief for {title}"
  - phase: "Main Edit"
    tasks:
      - "cut the first minute"
  - phase: "Other"
```

Every project from that template starts with the list, interpolated the way a
file name is. A block with no `phase` writes its tasks bare; a block with no
`tasks` writes the label alone, which is how you hand out an empty `### Other`.
A template with no `todo:` produces no section at all, exactly as before. The
gallery's music-video template now carries one.

## `{id}` resolves when a template is applied

`fastf apply` rendered `{id}` as the literal text `{id}`, silently — worst in
`fastf register --apply`, which runs apply moments after writing a fresh id to
disk. It now comes from the target folder's own `PROJECT_INFO.md`. A folder
fastf holds no metadata for has no number to give: the token stays as written,
and `apply` says so once instead of leaving it to be found later.
